finding.engine_off.title: Engine was not running during the scan
finding.engine_off.detail: Fault codes and identification are complete, but live engine values (fuel trims, sensors, charging) are only meaningful with the engine idling at normal temperature. Re-scan with the engine warm and idling for a full check.

finding.obd_pending.detail: Pending code: the fault was detected once but not yet confirmed. It may be an early sign of a developing problem.{also}
finding.obd_permanent.detail: Permanent codes clear themselves only after the car verifies the repair over several drive cycles.
finding.direct_state: The engine computer's direct read reports it as: {state}.
finding.dtc_unreadable.title: Could not read fault codes from {ecu}
finding.dtc_unreadable.detail: The module answered but refused the fault code request.
finding.ecu_code.title: {code}{ftb} ({state})
finding.silent.title: Some modules did not answer
finding.silent.detail: Not answering usually means the module is not fitted on this trim level: {modules}.
finding.network_event.title: Communication / supply-voltage codes stored in {n} module(s)
finding.network_event.detail: {listing}. None of them is active now. Modules store these codes when the supply voltage dips or they stop hearing each other for a moment: a weak or discharged battery, a jump start, cranking with a low battery, the battery disconnected with the ignition on, or a loose battery terminal or ground. A faulty module is the least likely cause. Test the battery and charging, check the terminals and grounds, then have the codes erased with a workshop tool. If they come back, look for a wiring or ground fault.
finding.vin_mismatch.title: Not every module reports the same VIN
finding.vin_mismatch.detail: {listing}. A different VIN usually means that module was replaced with a used part from another car. That often works fine, but some functions (immobilizer, keys, ABS or airbag coding) depend on it; mention it to the workshop.
finding.charging_low.title: Low charging voltage: {v:.1f} V with engine running
finding.charging_low.detail: With the engine running the alternator should hold 13.5-14.7 V. Possible weak alternator, slipping belt or bad connection.
finding.charging_high.title: High charging voltage: {v:.1f} V
finding.charging_high.detail: Above 15 V can damage the battery and electronics (voltage regulator).
finding.battery_low.title: Battery voltage low: {v:.1f} V (engine off)
finding.battery_low.detail: A fully charged battery rests at 12.6-12.8 V; 12.4 V is about 75 % charge. Below 12.0 V it is discharged or failing, which can also cause random electronic faults.
finding.battery_slightly_low.title: Battery slightly low: {v:.1f} V (engine off)
finding.battery_slightly_low.detail: A fully charged battery rests at 12.6-12.8 V; this reading is about 75 % charge or less, and right after driving it should read higher. Charge it fully and re-test it with the engine off for a few hours; if it stays below 12.5 V, have the battery load-tested.
finding.lean.title: Engine running lean: total fuel trim +{total:.0f}%
finding.lean.detail: The computer is adding fuel (short term {stft:+.1f}%, long term {ltft:+.1f}%). Typical causes: vacuum/intake air leak, dirty or faulty MAF/MAP sensor, weak fuel pump or clogged filter, dirty injectors.
finding.rich.title: Engine running rich: total fuel trim {total:.0f}%
finding.rich.detail: The computer is removing fuel (short term {stft:+.1f}%, long term {ltft:+.1f}%). Typical causes: leaking injector, high fuel pressure, faulty O2 or coolant temperature sensor, saturated EVAP canister.
finding.coolant_high.title: Coolant temperature high: {t} °C
finding.coolant_high.detail: Risk of overheating. Check coolant level, radiator fan operation and water pump.
finding.coolant_warm.title: Coolant temperature on the high side: {t} °C
finding.coolant_warm.detail: Watch the temperature gauge; check the fan switches on around 99-102 °C.
finding.thermostat.title: Engine not reaching temperature: {t} °C after {minutes} min
finding.thermostat.detail: Often a thermostat stuck open. Increases fuel consumption and wear.
finding.o2_lazy.title: Upstream O2 sensor shows little activity
finding.o2_lazy.detail: Bank 1 sensor 1 varied only {swing:.2f} V across {n} samples (a healthy sensor swings ~0.1-0.9 V). Confirm with a longer graph; a lazy sensor raises consumption and emissions.
finding.o2_mirror.title: Downstream O2 sensor mirrors the upstream one
finding.o2_mirror.detail: When the rear sensor switches like the front one, the catalytic converter may be losing efficiency. Watch for code P0420.
finding.idle.title: Idle speed unusual: {rpm:.0f} rpm
finding.idle.detail: Warm idle is normally ~750-850 rpm. Check for air leaks, dirty throttle body or electrical loads (A/C, fans) during the scan.
finding.cleared.title: Fault codes were cleared recently
finding.cleared.detail: Only {km} km / {warmups} warm-ups since the codes were last erased (a battery disconnect also does this). Existing problems may not have re-appeared yet; scan again after a week of driving.
finding.monitors.title: Self-tests not yet completed
finding.monitors.detail: These on-board self-tests have not finished since the last reset: {monitors}. Normal after clearing codes or a battery disconnect.
finding.mil_km.title: Driven {km} km with the check-engine light on
finding.mode06_fail.title: Self-test failed: {monitor} (test {tid})
finding.mode06_close.title: Self-test close to its limit: {monitor} (test {tid})
finding.mode06_close.detail: Passed, but within {margin}% of a limit. Could fail in the future.

finding.supply_low.title: A module measures a lower supply voltage than the OBD socket
finding.supply_low.detail: {listing}, against {ref:.1f} V at the OBD socket. More than 0.5 V lower usually means a poor ground or a corroded connector on that module's supply, a common cause of the voltage codes. Check its ground points and connector.
finding.batt_test_crank_weak.title: Battery weak when starting: dropped to {v:.1f} V
finding.batt_test_crank_weak.detail: A healthy battery stays above about 10 V while the engine starts; below 9.6 V it is failing or badly discharged. That alone can explain voltage codes in several modules. Charge it fully and have it load-tested; replace it if it fails.
finding.batt_test_brownout.title: Battery too weak to start cleanly: the adapter lost power
finding.batt_test_brownout.detail: The voltage dropped so low while starting that the OBD adapter itself restarted (usually below 7–8 V). The battery is failing or its connections are bad: check the terminals and the ground strap, then have the battery load-tested.
finding.batt_test_crank_fair.title: Battery borderline when starting: {v:.1f} V
finding.batt_test_crank_fair.detail: Between 9.6 and 10 V while starting: it still starts, but with little reserve, especially in cold weather. Recharge it and test again; plan a replacement if it stays here.
finding.batt_test_rest_low.title: Battery discharged at rest: {v:.1f} V
finding.batt_test_rest_low.detail: Below 12.4 V at rest the battery is under 75 % charged. Charge it fully (a long drive is often not enough) and test again; if it stays low, the battery is ageing or something drains it while parked.
finding.batt_test_rest_fair.title: Battery not fully charged at rest: {v:.1f} V
finding.batt_test_rest_fair.detail: 12.4–12.6 V at rest is about 75–100 % charge. Fine for now; if starting is ever slow, charge it fully and test again.
finding.batt_test_charge_low.title: Low charging voltage at idle: {v:.1f} V
finding.batt_test_charge_low.detail: With the engine idling the alternator should hold 13.5–14.8 V. Check the alternator belt, the alternator output and the cables between alternator, battery and ground.
finding.batt_test_charge_high.title: High charging voltage: {v:.1f} V
finding.batt_test_charge_high.detail: Above 14.8 V overcharges the battery and stresses the electronics; usually the alternator's voltage regulator.
finding.batt_test_load_low.title: Charging drops under load: {v:.1f} V (was {idle:.1f} V at idle)
finding.batt_test_load_low.detail: With lights, blower, defrost and A/C on, the voltage should stay above about 13.2 V. A bigger drop points to a weak alternator, a slipping belt or poor connections.
finding.batt_test_ok.title: Battery and charging test passed
finding.batt_test_ok.detail: At rest {rest:.1f} V, lowest while starting {crank:.1f} V, charging {idle:.1f} V: all within normal limits.
report.batt_note: Test made {at}. Measured at the OBD socket, about 0.1–0.3 V below the battery terminals.
report.module_partial: Standard scan: the {n} most informative of {total} readings were taken. A deep scan reads them all.
ui.odometer_hint_new: Lets the report say how long ago each fault code was stored. If a module reports the mileage (with the Renault database), the car's reading is used instead.
ui.odometer_hint_saved: Saved on {date}. Used only when no module reports the mileage; update it now and then, or clear it.
